name: STRIDE Security Threat Modeling Skill
description: Structured methodology and taxonomy schema for identifying security threats using Microsoft's STRIDE framework.
author: community

categories.name: Spoofing
categories.question: Can an attacker pretend to be a valid user, server, or process?

categories.name: Tampering
categories.question: Can an attacker modify data in transit, on disk, or in memory?

categories.name: Repudiation
categories.question: Can a bad actor deny performing an action without verifiable proof?

categories.name: Information Disclosure
categories.question: Can confidential data be exposed to unauthorized parties?

categories.name: Denial of Service
categories.question: Can a system be overwhelmed to deny service to legitimate users?

categories.name: Elevation of Privilege
categories.question: Can an unprivileged user execute admin actions or escape a sandbox?

execution_workflow: 1. Deconstruct system data flow diagram (DFD): External Entities, Processes, Data Stores, Data Flows.
2. Identify all Trust Boundaries across network layers.
3. Iterate through each STRIDE category per element crossing a trust boundary.
4. Calculate risk score using DREAD or CVSS v3.
